title: How Binance Replaced $6.3 Billion in Hours 🤯
alt_hooks: Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in the biggest crypto heist ever.
How did Binance replace $5.7 billion of stolen crypto in a single day?
When North Korea stole $6.3 billion, Binance did the unthinkable.

scenes.line: Hackers stole a record $6.3 billion from Binance in history's biggest crypto heist.

shots.words: from Binance in history's biggest crypto heist.

scenes.line: North Korean attackers drained user wallets within minutes using automated transfer scripts, leveraging a compromised employee laptop.

shots.words: North Korean attackers drained user wallets
within minutes using automated transfer scripts.

scenes.line: Co-CEO Richard Teng immediately tapped the billion dollar SAFU emergency fund, futures reserves, and corporate treasury.

shots.words: the billion dollar SAFU emergency fund

scenes.line: By Saturday morning, Dubai-based Binance used company money to buy back 90 percent of the assets from the market.

shots.words: By Saturday morning, Binance used company money
to buy back 90 percent of the assets.

scenes.line: Users bore zero financial impact as withdrawal services prepared to reopen on Sunday as scheduled.

shots.words: as withdrawal services prepared to reopen on Sunday.

scenes.line: Leaving hackers with a historic heist that the world's largest exchange absorbed almost overnight through transparent reporting.

shots.words: Leaving hackers with a historic heist
that the exchange absorbed almost overnight.

description: After hackers stole $6.3 billion in a massive crypto breach linked to North Korea, Binance CEO Richard Teng announced that 90% of the stolen assets were replenished using corporate treasuries and emergency funds, keeping user balances completely whole.
pinned: Would you trust an exchange that replaces a $6.3 billion hack overnight?
